source.title: Causal scrubbing: results on induction heads
source.authors: LawrenceC; Adrià Garriga-alonso; Nicholas Goldowsky-Dill; ryan_greenblatt; Tao Lin; jenny; Ansh Radhakrishnan; Buck; Nate Thomas

record.tranche_reason: The study causally tests an induction-head mechanism and finds the initial, narrow account inadequate, then refines it with additional information paths.
record.gate_note: Reports attention-pattern identification and causal-scrubbing outcomes on a single model. The cited induction-head paper's results are background, not this study's findings. The post says that evaluating the same experiments on all tokens lowers recovered loss relative to the induction-selected subset, but gives no amount.
record.test_reason: Causal-scrubbing tests of the induction mechanism in a 2-layer attention-only model. The authors find that the Olsson-style naive account (embeddings to Q/V, previous-token head to K) recovers only 35% of loss. More general hypotheses are needed to reach 86–91%.
record.authors_conclusion: Broadly correct. The authors say the naive, Olsson-style hypothesis explains only 35% of the loss. They say induction heads in small models draw on many information paths (self-attending layer-0 heads, the last three positions), not just previous-token heads and embeddings. Those paths can be narrowed considerably: a reasonably specific hypothesis recovers 86–89%, and a less specific one 91%.
record.recipe_differences: Uses causal scrubbing and resampling ablations to test mechanistic hypotheses about attention-head pathways, rather than the original studies' approach to identifying induction heads or tracking their formation and in-context-learning dynamics.
record.method_sensitivity: Evaluation on all tokens recovers less loss than evaluation on the induction-selected subset. The reported recovery also changes across the successive scrub hypotheses and the Q, K, V, and combined-path conditions.
record.problems: Evidence is from one 2-layer attention-only model and an evaluation subset selected for induction being useful; the post notes that results are lower when evaluated on all tokens but gives no magnitude. Uncertainty estimates are not reported. A comparison sentence for the refined-hypothesis-5 K result is internally inconsistent with the listed values.

untested.parts: Formation of the circuit, and any model other than this single 2-layer attention-only model.
All parts: no large models and no token-index loss.
All parts: no variation of data or training.
All parts: no few-shot task learning.

record.verdict_notes: Single model, evaluated on a whitelisted token subset chosen for induction being useful. No uncertainty is reported. Alignment Forum post, not peer reviewed. Neither original source is this study.

versions.untested_parts: Tests mechanism in one 2-layer attention-only model on a token subset selected for induction being useful. Does not test formation across multiple models, other sizes, or training runs.
No training-time formation, in-context-learning trajectory, or training-loss-curve measurement.
Does not measure most in-context learning or loss change with token index in large transformers.
No comparison across model families, sizes, runs, architectures, or modalities.
Does not vary training data or training setup; selecting evaluation tokens is not a training-data intervention.
No few-shot task-learning test or comparison with other mechanisms for that behavior.
Does not examine formation transitions or their timing.

relationships.condition: Heads 1.5/1.6, previous-token head 0.0, and refined hypotheses in the 2-layer attention-only OpenWebText model, on induction-selected tokens
relationships.reason: Induction heads show [A][B]…[A] attention (r2, r3) and matter for loss (0.160 vs 0.213, r1). Refined hypotheses that still route K through the previous-token head recover 86–91% (r20, r24, r28), with V at 97% (r11).
relationships.display_finding: Induction heads attended to matching continuations and affected loss, reported as 0.160 versus 0.213; refined hypotheses routing keys through the previous-token head recovered 86–91% of performance, with the value-path hypothesis recovering 97%.

source_check.label: supports
source_check.condition: Heads 1.5/1.6, previous-token head 0.0, and refined hypotheses in the 2-layer attention-only OpenWebText model, on induction-selected tokens
source_check.reason: Induction attention and causal contributions are observed; refined accounts retaining the previous-token-head pathway recover 86–91%. These accounts also allow other paths, so this does not establish that head 0.0 alone supplies the keys.

relationships.condition: Naive mechanism (Q and V from embeddings only, K from the previous-token head only)
relationships.reason: The naive account recovers only 35% combined (r8), with Q at 51% (r6) and K at 79% (r7). High recovery needs extra paths: self-attending layer-0 heads, the last three positions, and average layer-0 OV effects (r12, r16). Results drop when evaluated on all tokens (r29).
relationships.display_finding: The naive account recovered 35% overall, with query and key hypotheses recovering 51% and 79%, respectively; higher recovery required self-attending layer-0 heads, the last three positions, and average layer-0 OV effects, while evaluation across all tokens reduced recovery.

source_check.label: limits_scope
source_check.condition: Naive mechanism (Q and V from embeddings only, K from the previous-token head only)
source_check.reason: The naive combined hypothesis recovers 35%, with Q, K and V individually recovering 51%, 79% and 90%; additional pathways substantially improve recovery.

source_check.notes: Recovery percentages normalize the 0.053 loss difference, rather than total model loss; all-token recovery is reported only qualitatively. The introduction identifies this post as a detailed account of results also summarized in lw:JvZhhzycHu2Yd57RN, so those reports should not count as independent experiments.
